name: Ashline Bitters — The Shelf Aperitif
creator: Distillery collective Ruin & Proof, attributed to Joachim Seo-Abara
description: A charcoal-filtered, intensely bitter synth-grain spirit produced by Ruin & Proof, a Shelf-based distillery operating out of Ward 6 since 2196, Ashline Bitters became the defining aperitif of GLMZ's gray-market bar culture through a combination of aggressive flavor — it is genuinely difficult to drink straight — and a pricing structure that made it the cheapest available spirit in most unlicensed bars at Φ0.60 per measure. The signature serve is two fingers of Ashline over a single synth-ice cube with a preserved lemon peel, called simply 'a Shelf pour.' The distillery's founder, Joachim Seo-Abara, is rumored to have encoded the original formula in a physical notebook that has changed hands multiple times under disputed circumstances.
cultural_impact: Ashline Bitters underwent the peculiar cultural trajectory of being adopted upward — by 2210 it appeared on menus in Tier 3 and Tier 4 bars as a prestige item, priced at Φ8.00 per measure and described in tasting notes as 'confrontational.' This inversion delighted and infuriated Shelf drinkers in roughly equal measure and generated a countercultural movement to drink it only straight, without ice, as a form of authenticity declaration.
controversy: Ruin & Proof operates without a distilling license and has survived three separate HelixCorp compliance raids through a combination of community warning networks and the fact that their Ward 6 location is technically in a jurisdictional gap between two corponation infrastructure zones. A licensed spirits manufacturer, Helix Provision Beverage Group, released a product called Ashline Reserve in 2213 that Seo-Abara described as 'a photograph of something that was never photographed.'
story_hooks: The physical notebook containing the original Ashline formula has surfaced in a Tier 4 auction house, and Seo-Abara — who claims it was stolen — needs someone to retrieve it without triggering a legal process that would expose the distillery's unlicensed status.

A Tier 3 bar owner who built a profitable Ashline-focused menu is approached by Helix Provision Beverage Group to become a 'brand ambassador' — and must weigh the money against what it would mean in their community.

Three people in Ward 6 have developed an unusual neurochemical sensitivity that their doctors can only correlate with long-term Ashline consumption — and the formula notebook may contain an ingredient that Seo-Abara didn't know was dangerous.
